Magsasagawa ang Maynilad ng permanent road restoration sa kahabaan ng Payatas Road, mula Rose St. hanggang Payatas Bridge.

🗓 Simula: 10:00 PM, February 13, 2026
🗓 Hanggang: 5:00 AM, February 16, 2026

Sa mga araw na ito, asahan ang pagbagal at pagbigat ng daloy ng trapiko sa naturang lugar.

Magpapatupad ng stop-and-go traffic scheme habang isinasagawa ang road works. May nakahandang rerouting plan para sa mga motoristang manggagaling sa Batasan Road.

Pinapayuhan ang lahat na dumaan sa mga alternatibong ruta at maglaan ng dagdag na oras sa biyahe upang maiwasan ang abala.

Magtutulungan at nakaantabay ang mga tauhan ng Traffic and Transport Management Department (TTMD), Department of Public Order and Safety (DPOS), Task Force Disiplina, at Quezon City Police District (QCPD), para matiyak ang kaayusan ng daloy ng trapiko sa nasabing lugar.

Maraming salamat po sa inyong pag-unawa.

data.raw_text:
The reclaimed land where SM Mall of Asia, Solaire Resort and Casino, and City of Dreams stand is slowly collapsing under its own weight, according to a University of the Philippines Diliman study.

Using satellite data, researchers found that parts of the Manila Bay Freeport Zone, entirely built atop the ocean to meet real estate demand, are gradually sinking. Areas affected include SM Mall of Asia, City of Dreams, Solaire, and Seascape Village beside the now‑closed Sofitel. Visible cracks already mar the ground, signaling that these high‑profile developments may not be as permanent—or as safe—as advertised. 

Meanwhile, land reclamation continues in the same part of town. The Philippine Reclamation Authority has cleared or allowed projects like the Pasay Eco‑City coastal developments—including the 360‑hectare Pasay 360 plan linked to the MOA complex—to proceed, extending the coastline further into the bay even as the land beneath existing structures weakens.

Environmental advocates have long stood against reclamation because of its harmful effects on ocean health, aquatic life, and sanitation. Scientists also warn that reclamation worsens flooding for coastal communities. 

The study was originally published in 2023 but has resurfaced amid renewed calls from civil society groups to halt all government reclamation projects due to intense flooding and long‑term safety concerns. 

Report by Kiara Gorrospe
